title: World Cup 2026 betting pool
summary: A Mexican app expects 2 million players during the 2026 World Cup matches, and bets spike at minute 90.

requirements.1: {{s1}} is the HTTP proxy that receives bets over HTTPS, spreads the requests across the containers and passes the player's IP to the API in the X-Forwarded-For header.
requirements.2: {{s2}} runs the API in containers without the two-person team managing servers, nodes or a Kubernetes cluster.
requirements.3: {{s3}} keeps the leaderboard of 2 million players in memory, sorted by points, so the API does not hit the database on every lookup.
requirements.4: {{s4}} absorbs the minute-90 spike: workers pull bets at their own pace and each one is done only when they confirm they processed it; otherwise it is delivered again.
requirements.5: {{s5}} is the NoSQL store for the bets: it saves each one keyed by player and match and writes it only if that key does not exist yet, so nobody bets twice.
requirements.6: The score provider sends each goal to the slot 2 API, which updates the slot 3 leaderboard.

s1.explanation: The regional external Application Load Balancer is a layer 7 proxy for HTTP and HTTPS; with a serverless NEG it reaches Cloud Run in the same region and passes the player's IP in X-Forwarded-For.

s2.explanation: Cloud Run is a fully managed platform for running containers: there is no cluster to create or infrastructure to manage, and it scales with the requests.
s2.hint_cue: without the two-person team managing servers

s3.explanation: Memorystore for Valkey is a fully managed in-memory Valkey service that can be deployed in northamerica-south1 (Mexico); Google uses it as a caching layer to deliver real-time leaderboards.

s4.explanation: With a Pub/Sub pull subscription, workers request messages when they can and must acknowledge each one; if they do not ack it before the deadline, Pub/Sub delivers it again.

s5.explanation: Firestore is a NoSQL document database that scales with the load on its own. A write with the precondition that the document must not exist only applies if it is not there yet, so the bet is not duplicated.
s5.hint_cue: writes it only if that key does not exist yet

gcp-passthrough-nlb.s1: Passthrough Network Load Balancers do not support serverless NEGs, so they cannot send traffic to Cloud Run; also, the requirement asks for an HTTP proxy.

gcp-gke-standard.s2: In GKE Standard the team configures its own node pools and plans their capacity, and the requirement rules out running a Kubernetes cluster.

gcp-cloud-sql-read-replica.s3: A Cloud SQL read replica is a read-only copy of the relational database; the requirement asks to keep the leaderboard in memory.
gcp-cloud-sql-read-replica.s5: Cloud SQL read replicas are read-only: the bet cannot be written to them.

gcp-managed-kafka.s4: In Managed Service for Apache Kafka what a consumer group receives is controlled with the offsets of each partition, and Google recommends Pub/Sub when you need per-message processing tracking.

gcp-cloud-storage.s5: Cloud Storage stores immutable objects that do not change during their storage lifetime; the requirement asks for a NoSQL database.
